children.text: pīyūṣābhiniveśa eṣa rabhasād asmākam adyānayā
children.translated_text: This craving of ours for nectar, impetuous from the start, was today

children.text: bandhūkadyutibāndhavādhararasasyandena mandīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: dulled by the flowing essence of the lips, companions of the <s>bandhūka</s>-flower's radiance;

children.text: itthaṃ daityacayaḥ samudramathane yena kṣaṇād vañcitas
children.translated_text: thus in an instant was the host of demons deceived at the churning of the ocean —

children.text: tasmai sādaram oṃnamo 'stu kapaṭastrīrūpiṇe viṣṇave
children.translated_text: to that <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the deceptive form of a woman, I reverently bow!

children.text: pīyūṣa-abhiniveśa eṣa rabhasād asmākam adya anayā
bandhūka-dyuti-bāndhava-adhara-rasa-syandena mandīkṛtaḥ
itthaṃ daitya-cayaḥ samudra-mathane yena kṣaṇād vañcitas
tasmai sādaram oṃ-namo 'stu kapaṭa-strī-rūpiṇe viṣṇave
hāridradravasodarāya rasanāmaṃḍo(mātro)paristhāyine
children.translated_text: To you who are kin to a belly full of turmeric juice, who stand as merely a morsel on the tongue,

children.text: satyād anyatamāya vittaharaṇapratyakṣacaurāya ca
children.translated_text: who are another than truth, a manifest thief of wealth,

children.text: citraṃ durbhagarūpavarṇanamahāpāṇḍityavidyāya te
children.translated_text: wondrous! whose great erudition consists of describing the beauty of the ugly —

children.text: vyājānāṃ prathamāya garbhagaṇikārāgāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ
children.translated_text: to you who are the foremost of frauds, whose passion is that of a courtesan for her unborn child — I bow!

children.text: hāridra-drava-sodarāya rasanā-maṃḍo(mātro)paristhāyine
satyād anyatamāya vitta-haraṇa-pratyakṣa-caurāya ca
citraṃ durbhaga-rūpa-varṇana-mahā-pāṇḍitya-vidyāya te
vyājānāṃ prathamāya garbha-gaṇikā-rāgāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ
dhyānaṃ yat parameśvaraṃ prati sadā yad vītarāgaṃ mano
children.translated_text: The meditation that is always directed toward the Supreme Lord, the mind that is free from passion,

children.text: yat karmātikaṭhoraghoragahanaṃ bhūtyai yad atyādaraḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>karma</s> (action) that is exceedingly harsh and terrible, the devotion that aims at prosperity,

children.text: āścaryaṃ ca śarīradānam api yat kāryaṃ vikāraṃ vinā
children.translated_text: the wonder of offering even one's own body without any disturbance —

children.text: tad veśyaiva tapasvinī kaliyuge loko 'pi tadbhāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: in the <s>Kali</s> age, only the courtesan is such an ascetic, and the world too is devoted to her!

children.text: dhyānaṃ yat parameśvaraṃ prati sadā yad vīta-rāgaṃ mano
yat karma-atikaṭhora-ghora-gahanaṃ bhūtyai yad atyādaraḥ
āścaryaṃ ca śarīra-dānam api yat kāryaṃ vikāraṃ vinā
tad veśya aiva tapasvinī kali-yuge loko 'pi tad-bhāvitaḥ
śrīmantaṃ śirasā bibharti kurute viśvabhramaṃ helayā
children.translated_text: She bears the wealthy man on her head, creates universal bewilderment with ease,

children.text: dhatte pāṭakapakṣapātam aniśaṃ naivāmiśais tṛpyati
children.translated_text: constantly maintains bias toward the rogue, and is never satisfied with mere crumbs;

children.text: raktaṃ pātum apīhate ca sakalaṃ tārkṣyasya mūrtir yathā
children.translated_text: she thirsts to drink the blood of everything — just like the form of <s>Garuḍa</s> (the eagle),

children.text: veśyā kiṃ tu bhujaṅgabhakṣaṇavidhau nādyāpi viśrāmyati
children.translated_text: but the courtesan does not rest even now from the practice of devouring serpents!

children.text: śrīmantaṃ śirasā bibharti kurute viśva-bhramaṃ helayā
dhatte pāṭaka-pakṣa-pātam aniśaṃ na evā amiśais tṛpyati
raktaṃ pātum apī ihate ca sakalaṃ tārkṣyasya mūrtir yathā
veśyā kiṃ tu bhujaṅga-bhakṣaṇa-vidhau na adya api viśrāmyati
te gandharvapure vasantu vibhavaṃ svapnārjitaṃ bhuñjatāṃ
children.translated_text: Let them dwell in a city of <s>gandharvas</s> (illusion), let them enjoy wealth earned in dreams,

children.text: kurvantu kṣaṇam antarikṣakusumaiḥ sragdāmaśobhām api
children.translated_text: let them make for a moment a beautiful garland from sky-flowers —

children.text: veśyānāṃ śaśaśṛṅgabhaṅgisadṛśaṃ vāllabhyam āsādya ye
children.translated_text: those who, having obtained the favor of courtesans, like the curve of a hare's horn,

children.text: sarvasvakṣapaṇāya kevalam aho mūrkhāḥ sukhenāsate
children.translated_text: merely for the ruin of all their possessions — alas, the fools sit at ease!

children.text: te gandharva-pure vasantu vibhavaṃ svapna-arjitaṃ bhuñjatāṃ
kurvantu kṣaṇam antarikṣakusumaiḥ srag-dāma-śobhām api
veśyānāṃ śaśa-śṛṅga-bhaṅgi-sadṛśaṃ vāllabhyam āsādya ye
sarvasva-kṣapaṇāya kevalam aho mūrkhāḥ sukhena-āsate
śvaityaṃ kalpaya kajjale kapikuleṣv āropayācāpalaṃ
children.translated_text: Attribute whiteness to lampblack, impute steadiness to a tribe of monkeys,

children.text: kodaṇḍe janayārjavaṃ viracaya grāvṇāṃ gaṇe mārdavam
children.translated_text: produce straightness in a bow, create softness among a group of stones,

children.text: nimbe sādhaya mādhurīṃ surabhitām ādau rasone kuru
children.translated_text: achieve sweetness in the <s>nimba</s> (neem), make fragrance first in garlic —

children.text: premāṇaṃ gaṇikājane 'pi caturaḥ paścāt sakhe drakṣyasi
children.translated_text: if you are clever, friend, you will then see love in the courtesan-folk!

children.text: śvaityaṃ kalpaya kajjale kapi-kuleṣv āropaya acāpalaṃ
kodaṇḍe janaya arjavaṃ viracaya grāvṇāṃ gaṇe mārdavam
nimbe sādhaya mādhurīṃ surabhitām ādau rasa-ūne kuru
premāṇaṃ gaṇikā-jane 'pi caturaḥ paścāt sakhe drakṣyasi
kālaś cet karuṇāparaḥ kaliyugaṃ yady adya dharmapriyaṃ
children.translated_text: If Time is compassionate, if the <s>Kali</s> age is devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nistriṃśo yadi peśalo viṣadharaḥ saṃtoṣadāyī yadi
children.translated_text: if a sword is gentle, if a venomous snake bestows contentment,

children.text: agniś ced atiśītalaḥ khalajanaḥ sarvopakārī sa ced
children.translated_text: if fire is exceedingly cold, if a wicked man is beneficent to all,

children.text: āyuṣyaṃ yadi vā bhaviṣyati viṣaṃ veśyāpi tadrāgiṇī
children.translated_text: or if poison becomes life-giving — then the courtesan too is genuinely enamored!

children.text: kālaś cet karuṇā-paraḥ kali-yugaṃ yady adya dharma-priyaṃ
nistriṃśo yadi peśalo viṣadharaḥ saṃtoṣadāyī yadi
agniś ced atiśītalaḥ khala-janaḥ sarva-upakārī sa ced
āyuṣyaṃ yadi vā bhaviṣyati viṣaṃ veśyāpi tad-rāgiṇī
mūḍho nirvyasano vaṇig vikapaṭo rājādhikārī śuciḥ
children.translated_text: A fool without vices, a merchant without deceit, a royal officer who is pure,

children.text: svādhīno bhṛtako jaḍo guṇarataś cauro vyapetaspṛhaḥ
children.translated_text: an independent servant, a dullard who delights in virtues, a thief free from desire,

children.text: bhītaḥ śāntamatir vitaḥ savinayaḥ karṇejapo dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: a timid man of peaceful mind, a dandy with modesty, a whisperer who is righteous —

children.text: kiṃ kutrāpi kadāpi ko 'pi bhavitā veśyājano rāgavān
children.translated_text: will any of these ever be found anywhere? And will the courtesan-folk ever be truly in love?

children.text: mūḍho nirvyasano vaṇig vikapaṭo rāja-adhikārī śuciḥ
svādhīno bhṛtako jaḍo guṇa-rataś cauro vyapeta-spṛhaḥ
bhītaḥ śānta-matir vitaḥ sa-vinayaḥ karṇejapo dhārmikaḥ
kiṃ kutra api kada āpi ko 'pi bhavitā veśyā-jano rāgavān
kāmo nāsti napuṃsakasya kulaṭāvargasya nāsti trapā
children.translated_text: Desire does not exist in the eunuch, shame does not exist in the class of unchaste women,

children.text: toyaṃ nāsti marīcikāsu satataṃ nāsti sthiratvaṃ śriyaḥ
children.translated_text: water does not exist in mirages, stability of wealth never exists,

children.text: dharmo nāsti ca nāstikasya vibhavo nāsti pramattātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> does not exist for the atheist, prosperity does not exist for the negligent,

children.text: snehānāṃ kaṇikāpi nāsti gaṇikālokasya ca prāyaśaḥ
children.translated_text: and not even a drop of affection exists in the world of courtesans, as a rule.

children.text: kāmo na asti napuṃsakasya kulaṭā-vargasya na asti trapā
toyaṃ na asti marīcikāsu satataṃ na asti sthiratvaṃ śriyaḥ
dharmo na asti ca nāstikasya vibhavo na asti pramatta-ātmanaḥ
snehānāṃ kaṇika āpi na asti gaṇikā-lokasya ca prāyaśaḥ
aśvīye yamavāhanasya nakulasyāśīviṣāṇāṃ kule
children.translated_text: The affection of <s>Aśvinī</s> (the mare) toward <s>Yama</s>'s vehicle (the buffalo), of the mongoose toward venomous serpents,

children.text: mārjārasya ca mūṣakeṣu ghaṭate yā prītir ātyantikī
children.translated_text: of the cat toward mice — that absolute love [that exists between natural enemies] —

children.text: kṣīṇe 'rthe vidhureṣu bandhuṣu dṛḍhe lokāpavāde śanair
children.translated_text: when wealth is exhausted, among distressed relatives, when public disgrace is firmly [established], gradually

children.text: jñeyā kāmijaneṣu saiva gaṇikāvargasya naisargikī
children.translated_text: know that same [hostile love] to be the natural [disposition] of the courtesan-class toward lovers.

children.text: aśvīye yama-vāhanasya nakulasyā aśīviṣāṇāṃ kule
mārjārasya ca mūṣakeṣu ghaṭate yā prītir ātyantikī
kṣīṇe 'rthe vidhureṣu bandhuṣu dṛḍhe loka-apavāde śanair
jñeyā kāmi-janeṣu sa aiva gaṇikā-vargasya naisargikī
yad yūtena yudhiṣṭhirasya vihitaṃ yad viṣṇunā vā baler
children.translated_text: What <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> did through gambling, what <s>Viṣṇu</s> did to <s>Bali</s>,

children.text: yac chukreṇa dhanādhipasya kalinā rājño nalasyāpi yat
children.translated_text: what <s>Śukra</s> [did] to the lord of wealth [<s>Kubera</s>], what <s>Kali</s> [did] to king <s>Nala</s>,

children.text: saṃbhūyāpi ca yat surāsurabalair unmathya pāthonidher
children.translated_text: and what the combined forces of gods and demons did by churning the ocean —

children.text: veśyā paśyata līlayaiva kurute tat tad gṛhe kāminām
children.translated_text: behold! The courtesan does all that effortlessly, right in the house of lovers!

children.text: yad yūtena yudhiṣṭhirasya vihitaṃ yad viṣṇunā vā baler
yac chukreṇa dhanādhipasya kalinā rājño nalasya api yat
saṃbhūya api ca yat sura-asura-balair unmathya pāthonidher
veśyā paśyata līlaya aiva kurute tat tad gṛhe kāminām
vākśurasya raṇo 'vadhiḥ kutanayotpattiḥ kulasyāvadhir
children.translated_text: The limit of a braggart is battle, the limit of a lineage is the birth of a bad son,

children.text: bāndhavyasya vivādabhūmir avadhiḥ saukhyaṃ śrutasy avadhiḥ
children.translated_text: the limit of kinship is a ground of quarrel, happiness is the limit of learning,

children.text: vācāṭasya vidagdhaparṣad avadhir laulyaṃ vratasyāvadhir
children.translated_text: for a prattler the limit is an assembly of the wise, fickleness is the limit of vows,

children.text: bandho viddhi dhanāvasānam avadhir veśyānurāgasya ca
children.translated_text: and know that bondage — the exhaustion of wealth — is the limit of attachment to courtesans.

children.text: vāk-śurasya raṇo 'vadhiḥ kutanaya-utpattiḥ kulasya avadhir
bāndhavyasya vivāda-bhūmir avadhiḥ saukhyaṃ śrutasy avadhiḥ
vācāṭasya vidagdha-parṣad avadhir laulyaṃ vratasya avadhir
bandho viddhi dhana-avasānam avadhir veśyā-anurāgasya ca
svāmī krūram ivāśritaṃ pariṇato yogīva saṃsāriṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Like a cruel master [regarding] a dependent, like a perfected <s>yogin</s> [regarding] a worldling,

children.text: śuddho vipra ivāntyajaṃ janapadaḥ śrīmān iva śvitriṇam
children.translated_text: like a pure <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [regarding] an outcaste, like a country lord [regarding] a leper,

children.text: dāsīputram ivoddhataḥ kuladharo nīco dhanīvārthinaṃ
children.translated_text: like an arrogant householder [regarding] a slave's son, like a lowly rich man [regarding] a beggar —

children.text: paryante tṛṇatulyam eva gaṇikā niḥsvaṃ janaṃ paśyanti
children.translated_text: in the end, the courtesan regards the penniless man as nothing more than a blade of grass.

children.text: svāmī krūram ivā aśritaṃ pariṇato yogi īva saṃsāriṇaṃ
śuddho vipra iva antyajaṃ jana-padaḥ śrīmān iva śvitriṇam
dāsī-putram iva uddhataḥ kula-dharo nīco dhani īva arthinaṃ
paryante tṛṇa-tulyam eva gaṇikā niḥsvaṃ janaṃ paśyanti
vipro dakṣiṇayā mahaiḥ parijano meghodayaiḥ kārṣiko
children.translated_text: The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is pleased by the sacrificial fee, the retinue by presents, the farmer by the rising of clouds,

children.text: durmantrī vyasanena sāhasaśataiḥ śūro mṛgair lubdhakaḥ
children.translated_text: the wicked counselor by calamity, the hero by hundreds of daring feats, the hunter by deer,

children.text: bandī tyāgibhir akṣarair janayitā lābhātirekair vaṇig
children.translated_text: the bard by generous patrons, the father by profits, the merchant by excess gains,

children.text: rogārtair bhiṣag arbhakaiś ca gaṇikā garbheśvarais tuṣyati
children.translated_text: the physician by the afflicted, and the courtesan — by children who are lords of wealth!

children.text: vipro dakṣiṇayā mahaiḥ parijano megha-udayaiḥ kārṣiko
durmantrī vyasanena sāhasa-śataiḥ śūro mṛgair lubdhakaḥ
bandī tyāgibhir akṣarair janayitā lābha-atirekair vaṇig
roga-artair bhiṣag arbhakaiś ca gaṇikā garbha-īśvarais tuṣyati
ajñānaḥ kalahaiḥ subhāṣitapadaiḥ sabhyo 'dhamaṛṇair dhanī
children.translated_text: The ignorant one plays with quarrels, the cultured one with well-spoken words, the rich one with bad debts,

children.text: jīvaiḥ śākuniko durodarakaraḥ śārair yamaḥ prāṇibhiḥ
children.translated_text: the fowler with [caught] birds, the gambler with dice, <s>Yama</s> with living beings,

children.text: grāmīṇair viṭapeṭakaḥ parijanaiḥ svāmī śiśuḥ kandukaiḥ
children.translated_text: the villager's pimp with his retinue, the master with servants, the child with balls —

children.text: śrīputrais taruṇais tathā navanavair vārāṅganā krīḍati
children.translated_text: and the courtesan plays with young sons of wealth, ever fresh and new!

children.text: ajñānaḥ kalahaiḥ subhāṣita-padaiḥ sabhyo 'dhama-ṛṇair dhanī
jīvaiḥ śākuniko durodarakaraḥ śārair yamaḥ prāṇibhiḥ
grāmīṇair viṭa-peṭakaḥ parijanaiḥ svāmī śiśuḥ kandukaiḥ
śrīputrais taruṇais tathā nava-navair vārāṅganā krīḍati
bhṛtyaḥ kuprabhusevayā narapatiḥ svacchandatādurnayair
children.translated_text: A servant is quickly cast down by serving a bad master, a king by willful misrule,

children.text: hevākena kavir madena kulajaḥ krodhāgninā tāpasaḥ
children.translated_text: a poet by contempt, a nobleman by intoxication, an ascetic by the fire of anger,

children.text: yogī bhogaviśeṣalampaṭatayā rogī kupathyāśanaī
children.translated_text: a <s>yogin</s> by greed for special pleasures, a sick man by eating unwholesome food,

children.text: rāgī catvarakāminīparicayaiḥ kṣiprād adhaḥ kṣipyate
children.translated_text: and the lover — by the company of streetwise courtesans — is swiftly cast downward!

children.text: bhṛtyaḥ kuprabhu-sevayā narapatiḥ svacchandatā-durnayair
hevākena kavir madena kulajaḥ krodha-agninā tāpasaḥ
yogī bhoga-viśeṣa-lampaṭatayā rogī kupathya-aśanaī
rāgī catvara-kāminī-paricayaiḥ kṣiprād adhaḥ kṣipyate
śālīnāṃ śalabhavrajo dhuṇagaṇo vaṃśapratānonnater
children.translated_text: A swarm of moths [is the ruin] of rice paddies, a host of termites of the spreading bamboo,

children.text: mattebhaḥ kamalākarasya kusumodyānasya durmārutaḥ
children.translated_text: a rutting elephant of the lotus pond, a fierce wind of the flower garden,

children.text: svasbhānur vidhumaṇḍalasya vaḍavāvakro nidher ambhasā
children.translated_text: <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>) of the moon's orb, the submarine fire of the ocean's waters —

children.text: māsāṃ kāmukasaṃpadāṃ ca gaṇikākṣudraḥ kīlopadravaḥ
children.translated_text: and the wretched, trifling courtesan — the pest of the month and of the lover's fortunes!

children.text: śālīnāṃ śalabha-vrajo dhuṇa-gaṇo vaṃśa-pratāna-unnater
matta-ibhaḥ kamala-ākarasya kusuma-udyānasya durmārutaḥ
svas-bhānur vidhu-maṇḍalasya vaḍavā-vakro nidher ambhasā
māsāṃ kāmuka-saṃpadāṃ ca gaṇikā-kṣudraḥ kīla-upadravaḥ
śauryasyātivikatthanaṃ ripunatir mānasya duḥśīlatā
children.translated_text: Excessive boasting is [the ruin] of valor, hostility of honor, immorality of character,

children.text: saundaryasya samunnates taralatā jñānasya garvagrahaḥ
children.translated_text: fickleness of the height of beauty, pride of knowledge, the seizure of arrogance,

children.text: aiśvaryasya vikāratā mukharatā vidyāprakarṣasya ca
children.translated_text: corruption of lordship, garrulity of the excellence of learning —

children.text: bhrātarvibhramanarmaṇaś ca gaṇikā sarvātmanā dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: and, brother, the courtesan is entirely the ruin of amorous sport!

children.text: śauryasya ativikatthanaṃ ripu-natir mānasya duḥśīlatā
saundaryasya samunnates taralatā jñānasya garva-grahaḥ
aiśvaryasya vikāratā mukharatā vidyā-prakarṣasya ca
bhrātar-vibhrama-narmaṇaś ca gaṇikā sarva-ātmanā dūṣaṇam
cchāyām abhradalaiḥ khalaiḥ sujanatāṃ mānonnatiṃ yācñayā
children.translated_text: He who seeks shade from wisps of cloud, kindness from rogues, elevation of honor through begging,

children.text: kārpaṇyena yaśāṃsi dhūrtakalayā maitrīṃ sukhaṃ sevayā
children.translated_text: fame through miserliness, friendship through the conduct of a cheat, happiness through servitude,

children.text: dharmaṃ prāṇivadhena vāñchati dhanaṃ dyūtaprasādeba yo
children.translated_text: <s>dharma</s> through killing living beings, and desires wealth through the grace of gambling,

children.text: veśyābhiś ca vilāsam ātmani narākāro 'sti gaur eva saḥ
children.translated_text: and dalliance with courtesans — though in human form, he is indeed a bull!

children.text: cchāyām abhra-dalaiḥ khalaiḥ sujanatāṃ māna-unnatiṃ yācñayā
kārpaṇyena yaśāṃsi dhūrta-kalayā maitrīṃ sukhaṃ sevayā
dharmaṃ prāṇivadhena vāñchati dhanaṃ dyūta-prasādeba yo
veśyābhiś ca vilāsam ātmani nara-ākāro 'sti gaur eva saḥ
nāndho mūrkhasamo na sevakasamo duḥkhī na yakṣmopamo
children.translated_text: No blind man equals the fool, no misery equals the servant's, no disease equals consumption,

children.text: vyādhir nādhir asatsutapratinidhis trāso na bhṛtyoḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: no enemy equals a wicked son, no terror equals the servant's;

children.text: kaṣṭaṃ nādhvasamānam indriyasamo nāriḥ parastrīsamaṃ
children.translated_text: no hardship equals the road, no foe equals the senses, no [danger] equals another's wife,

children.text: nānāyuṣyam avaśyanindyam atha no veśyāsamaṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: and nothing equals the courtesan that is assuredly to be censured and [yet] life-shortening.

children.text: na andho mūrkha-samo na sevaka-samo duḥkhī na yakṣma-upamo
vyādhir nādhir asat-suta-pratinidhis trāso na bhṛtyoḥ samaḥ
kaṣṭaṃ na adhva-samānam indriya-samo nāriḥ para-strī-samaṃ
na anāyuṣyam avaśya-nindyam atha no veśyā-samaṃ dṛśyate
kiṃ kāko 'pi vihaṃgamo marur api sthānaṃ karīro 'pi kiṃ
children.translated_text: Is a crow also a bird? Is a desert also a place? Is a <s>karīra</s> (thorny shrub) also

children.text: śākhī rāhur api grahaḥ sa ca bhaved uṣṭro 'pi kiṃ vā[ha]tam
children.translated_text: a tree? Is <s>Rāhu</s> also a planet? Is a camel also a [true] mount?

children.text: kiṃ kāco 'pi maṇir mṛgo 'pi karaṭiḥ preṣyo 'pi vā mānuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Is glass also a jewel? Is a [wild] animal also an elephant? Is a menial also a human being?

children.text: kiṃ veśyāpi vilāsinī sa ca tadāsakto 'pi kiṃ kāmukaḥ
children.translated_text: Is a courtesan also a charming woman? And is one attached to her also a lover?

children.text: kiṃ kāko 'pi vihaṃgamo marur api sthānaṃ karīro 'pi kiṃ
śākhī rāhur api grahaḥ sa ca bhaved uṣṭro 'pi kiṃ vā[ha]tam
kiṃ kāco 'pi maṇir mṛgo 'pi karaṭiḥ preṣyo 'pi vā mānuṣaḥ
kiṃ veśyā āpi vilāsinī sa ca tad-āsakto 'pi kiṃ kāmukaḥ
kiṃ tat karma yad astaśarma rasanā kiṃ sā na (ca) yāruṃtudā
children.translated_text: What is that action that destroys happiness? What is that tongue that wounds?

children.text: kiṃ tat prema yad asthiraṃ sa ca pumān kiṃ nāma yo nirguṇaḥ
children.translated_text: What is that love that is unstable? What is that man who is devoid of virtues?

children.text: sā kiṃ śrīr upabhogam arhati na yā sevyaḥ sa kiṃ yo 'ntaraṃ
children.translated_text: What is that prosperity that does not deserve enjoyment? Who is that person not worth serving who does not know

children.text: no jānāti tad asti kiṃ vilasitaṃ veśyāsu yat kṛtrimam
children.translated_text: any difference? Does any playfulness exist in courtesans that is not artificial?

children.text: kiṃ tat karma yad asta-śarma rasanā kiṃ sā na (ca) yāruṃtudā
kiṃ tat prema yad asthiraṃ sa ca pumān kiṃ nāma yo nirguṇaḥ
sā kiṃ śrīr upabhogam arhati na yā sevyaḥ sa kiṃ yo 'ntaraṃ
no jānāti tad asti kiṃ vilasitaṃ veśyāsu yat kṛtrimam
dūre tāni dhanāni yeṣu malanaṃ mānasya saṃjāyate
children.translated_text: Far be those riches from which arises the stain of pride!

children.text: bandhuḥ sa astu sukhī mukhe madhumayo yo 'ntaś ca māyāmayaḥ
children.translated_text: Let that friend be well whose mouth is full of honey but whose interior is full of deceit!

children.text: bhogāḥ pralayaṃ prayāntu katham apy aucityabhaṅgena ye
children.translated_text: Let those pleasures perish that involve the breach of propriety!

children.text: yāyātur nidhanaṃ varaṃ nidhuvanaṃ veśyāsu mūlyena yat
children.translated_text: Better die than have love-making with courtesans purchased with money!

children.text: dūre tāni dhanāni yeṣu malanaṃ mānasya saṃjāyate
bandhuḥ sa astu sukhī mukhe madhumayo yo 'ntaś ca māyāmayaḥ
bhogāḥ pralayaṃ prayāntu katham apy aucitya-bhaṅgena ye
yāyātur nidhanaṃ varaṃ nidhuvanaṃ veśyāsu mūlyena yat
asthānābhiniveśitā ratipater aucityabhaṅgo rater
children.translated_text: A misplaced investment of the god of love, a breach of propriety in love-making,

children.text: vaiyarthyaṃ navayauvanasya kim api premṇaḥ kalaṅkāṅkuraḥ
children.translated_text: the futility of fresh youth, the seedling of a blemish upon love,

children.text: saubhāgyasya vimānanā viguṇatā saundaryasāraśriyaḥ
children.translated_text: the dishonoring of good fortune, the flawing of the essence of beauty's splendor,

children.text: śṛṅgārasya viḍambanā kim aparaṃ veśyārataḍambaraḥ
children.translated_text: a travesty of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) — what else is the spectacle of love with courtesans?

children.text: asthāna-abhiniveśitā rati-pater aucitya-bhaṅgo rater
vaiyarthyaṃ nava-yauvanasya kim api premṇaḥ kalaṅka-aṅkuraḥ
saubhāgyasya vimānanā viguṇatā saundarya-sāra-śriyaḥ
śṛṅgārasya viḍambanā kim aparaṃ veśyā-rata-ḍambaraḥ
kruddho yasya manobhavas taruṇimā yenātmano vañcitas
children.translated_text: He upon whom <s>Manobhava</s> (<s>Kāma</s>, the love god) is angry, whose youth has deceived him,

children.text: tais tair yaś ca kaṭākṣitaḥ paribhavaiḥ sākṣād alakṣmīmukhaiḥ
children.translated_text: who is glanced at by those side-long looks that are directly the faces of misfortune,

children.text: yuktāyuktavicāraṇāparihṛtaḥ kāmaṃ sa kāmī krimiḥ
children.translated_text: who is deprived of the discrimination between right and wrong — that lover is indeed a worm!

children.text: paṇyastrīṣu nitambanāmani mahānimbe ratiṃ vindati
children.translated_text: He finds delight in courtesan-women, in that great <s>nimba</s> (neem tree) called 'buttocks'!

children.text: kruddho yasya manobhavas taruṇimā yenā atmano vañcitas
tais tair yaś ca kaṭākṣitaḥ paribhavaiḥ sākṣād alakṣmī-mukhaiḥ
yukta-ayukta-vicāraṇā-parihṛtaḥ kāmaṃ sa kāmī krimiḥ
paṇya-strīṣu nitamba-nāmani mahā-nimbe ratiṃ vindati
śāpaḥ ko 'pi mahānayaṃ pariṇatir duṣkarmaṇām īdṛśī
children.translated_text: Some great curse is this! This is the fruit of wicked deeds!

children.text: daurjanyaṃ paramaṃ vidher idam iyaṃ sākṣād alakṣmī sthirā
children.translated_text: This is the supreme villainy of fate! This is <s>Alakṣmī</s> (misfortune) herself, permanent!

children.text: sauhārdasya ca vibhramasya ca rater bhartuś ca yūnāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Of affection and of pleasure and of love and of the master and of the young —

children.text: yat saṃtyajya kulāṅganāṃ bahumukho dāsījanaḥ sevyate
children.translated_text: [what a travesty] that, abandoning a woman of good family, the servant-folk with many faces is served!

children.text: śāpaḥ ko 'pi mahānayaṃ pariṇatir duṣkarmaṇām īdṛśī
daurjanyaṃ paramaṃ vidher idam iyaṃ sākṣād alakṣmī sthirā
sauhārdasya ca vibhramasya ca rater bhartuś ca yūnāṃ tathā
yat saṃtyajya kula-aṅganāṃ bahu-mukho dāsī-janaḥ sevyate
saṃparko 'py atikarkaśaḥ paricayābhāso 'py asaṃpatkaro
children.translated_text: Even contact [with courtesans] is exceedingly harsh, even the semblance of acquaintance brings no fortune,

children.text: dṛkpāto 'py avasādasūr api sakṛt saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: even a glance causes ruin, even a single conversation is a corruption,

children.text: chāyāpi cchalanātmikā parimalodgāro 'pi hālāhalaṃ
children.translated_text: even a shadow is deceitful by nature, even the emanation of fragrance is poison (<s>hālāhala</s>) —

children.text: veśyānāṃ viṣayeṣu kiṃ puno 'ho saktir mahāsāhasam
children.translated_text: regarding the matters of courtesans, what more [need be said]? Alas, attachment to them is a great recklessness!

children.text: saṃparko 'py atikarkaśaḥ paricaya-ābhāso 'py asaṃpat-karo
dṛkpāto 'py avasādasūr api sakṛt saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ dūṣaṇam
chāya āpi cchalana-ātmikā parimala-udgāro 'pi hālāhalaṃ
veśyānāṃ viṣayeṣu kiṃ puno 'ho saktir mahā-sāhasam
droho yasya pitā kalāḥ kila catuḥṣaṣṭis tathā mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: Treachery is its father, the sixty-four arts are its mothers indeed,

children.text: prāṇāḥ sarvam alīkam arthaharaṇaṃ nāma pradhānavratam
children.translated_text: life-breaths are entirely false, the chief vow is the seizure of wealth,

children.text: vikreyaṃ nijam aṅgam aṅgam api cānaṅgaḥ sahāyaḥ svayaṃ
children.translated_text: its own body is for sale limb by limb, and <s>Anaṅga</s> (<s>Kāma</s>, the bodiless love god) himself is its ally —

children.text: tasyānarthaśatātmakasya gaṇikāvyādheḥ kim asty auṣadham
children.translated_text: for that disease of the courtesan, consisting of a hundred calamities, what medicine exists?

children.text: droho yasya pitā kalāḥ kila catuḥṣaṣṭis tathā mātaraḥ
prāṇāḥ sarvam alīkam artha-haraṇaṃ nāma pradhāna-vratam
vikreyaṃ nijam aṅgam aṅgam api ca anaṅgaḥ sahāyaḥ svayaṃ
tasya anartha-śata-ātmakasya gaṇikā-vyādheḥ kim asty auṣadham
gṛdhrī nirbharam āmiṣeṣu saraghā ghorā madhūnāṃ bhare
children.translated_text: Greedy without restraint for flesh, a fierce bee [draining] the load of honeys,

children.text: tīkṣṇanakhakṣateṣu bhujagī daṃśaprakāreṣu ca
children.translated_text: In sharp nail-scratches, she is a serpent-woman with various biting techniques,

children.text: uttāneṣu vivartaneṣu śaphari vittacchale mūṣikā
children.translated_text: in upturned and inverted movements she is a fish, in stealing wealth she is a mouse —

children.text: veśyā kāmukavañcanāya bhuvane rūpair anekaiḥ sthitā
children.translated_text: the courtesan stands in the world with many forms, for the deception of lovers.

children.text: gṛdhrī nirbharam āmiṣeṣu saraghā ghorā madhūnāṃ bhare
tīkṣṇa-nakha-kṣateṣu bhujagī daṃśa-prakāreṣu ca
uttāneṣu vivartaneṣu śaphari vitta-cchale mūṣikā
veśyā kāmuka-vañcanāya bhuvane rūpair anekaiḥ sthitā
sāmrājyaṃ madhumāṃsamatsyagilanaṃ mantrī jaratkuṭṭanī
children.translated_text: Her sovereignty is the swallowing of liquor, meat, and fish; her minister is an aged procuress;

children.text: daṇḍyaḥ sārthakirāṭasūnuradhanāḥ śṛṅgāriṇaḥ kiṅkarāḥ
children.translated_text: her criminals are the merchant, the cheat, and the son; the impoverished are the amorous servants;

children.text: ācāro bahugālidānam adhamo mitraṃ dhanaṃ jīvitaṃ
children.translated_text: her custom is the giving of abundant abuse; her worst friend is wealth; her life —

children.text: veśyānāṃ puracāra ... tha bhagnaḥ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: the public conduct of courtesans... the beloved is broken.

children.text: sāmrājyaṃ madhu-māṃsa-matsya-gilanaṃ mantrī jarat-kuṭṭanī
daṇḍyaḥ sārtha-kirāṭasūnuradhanāḥ śṛṅgāriṇaḥ kiṅkarāḥ
ācāro bahu-gāli-dānam adhamo mitraṃ dhanaṃ jīvitaṃ
veśyānāṃ puracāra ... tha bhagnaḥ priyaḥ
rāgīti pratipattibhūr vita iti prāpto 'tivandyaṃ padaṃ
children.translated_text: 'A passionate one!' — thus he becomes a ground for solicitation; 'a libertine!' — thus he has attained a most venerable status;

children.text: ślāghārho vyasanīti hīnakula ity agryaḥ kuṭumbaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: 'praiseworthy!' — 'an addict!' — 'of low birth!' — yet he is himself the foremost of the household;

children.text: mānyaḥ prāhata ity aho kitava ity āptaś ca kiṃ vādhikaṃ
children.translated_text: 'respectable!' — 'a spendthrift!' — 'oh, what a gambler!' — 'a trustworthy man!' — and what more?

children.text: sarvāvastha iti pramāṇapuruṣo veśyābhir abhyarcyate
children.translated_text: 'A man for all occasions!' — thus the man of measure is worshipped by courtesans.

children.text: rāgi īti pratipatti-bhūr vita iti prāpto 'tivandyaṃ padaṃ
ślāgha-arho vyasani īti hīna-kula ity agryaḥ kuṭumbaḥ svayam
mānyaḥ prāhata ity aho kitava ity āptaś ca kiṃ va ādhikaṃ
sarva-avastha iti pramāṇa-puruṣo veśyābhir abhyarcyate
māṃspākotkaṭamadyagandhi viharacceṭīnaṭīsaṃkulaṃ
children.translated_text: Stinking of meat cooking and strong liquor, bustling with slave-girls and dancing-girls —

children.text: yad veśyāyatanaṃ bhujaṃga parayā bhaktyā puraḥ paśyasi
children.translated_text: O naive one, that courtesan's abode which you behold with supreme devotion before you —

children.text: atrāste gṛhadevatā vidadhatī digghaṭṭanaṃ kuṭṭanī
children.translated_text: therein dwells the household deity: the procuress, causing commotion in all directions,

children.text: yasyāḥ pratyaham āḍhyakāmukapaśuvrātopahārair baliḥ
children.translated_text: to whom daily offerings are made with sacrificial gifts of herds of wealthy amorous victims.

children.text: māṃspāka-utkaṭa-madya-gandhi viharac-ceṭī-naṭī-saṃkulaṃ
yad veśyā-āyatanaṃ bhujaṃga parayā bhaktyā puraḥ paśyasi
atrā aste gṛha-devatā vidadhatī dig-ghaṭṭanaṃ kuṭṭanī
yasyāḥ pratyaham āḍhya-kāmuka-paśu-vrāta-upahārair baliḥ

body.text: 32a: on māṃspākā see Pāṇini 6.1.144: aparasaparāḥ kriyāsātatye

children.text: pratyaṅgārpaṇacārucāṭukaraṇapremocitaprārthanā
children.translated_text: The offering of each limb, the making of charming flattery, the entreaty befitting love,

children.text: śrīvātāyanadarśanādigaṇikālokasya dharmaḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: the display from the auspicious window, and so on — this is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of the courtesan's world;

children.text: kuṭṭanyāḥ puna utkaṭotkaṭam idaṃ tatrāsty agastyavrataṃ
children.translated_text: but the procuress has something more intense than all that — there is her <s>Agastya</s>-vow,

children.text: yat prāṇāhutir ekakaiva sakalaī ratnākaraiḥ kāmibhiḥ
children.translated_text: whereby the single offering of life-breath [is consumed whole] by lovers who are entire mines of gems.

children.text: pratyaṅga-arpaṇa-cāru-cāṭu-karaṇa-prema-ucita-prārthanā
śrī-vātāyana-darśana-ādi-gaṇikā-lokasya dharmaḥ paraḥ
kuṭṭanyāḥ puna utkaṭa-utkaṭam idaṃ tatra asty agastya-vrataṃ
yat prāṇa-āhutir ekaka aiva sakalaī ratna-ākaraiḥ kāmibhiḥ
kandarpapratibhūniveśitavalīrekhāvalīśobhite
children.translated_text: On the broad hip-surface of courtesans, adorned with rows of folds deposited as pledges by <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love),

children.text: līlodañcitabāhupāśayugalāpātaiś ca bhoḥ kāmukāḥ
children.translated_text: and with the casts of the paired nooses of arms playfully raised — O lovers!

children.text: veśyānāṃ vipule nitambaphalake śāraiḥ kaṭākṣair ito
children.translated_text: that game which you have played here with the arrows of sidelong glances

children.text: yad vaḥ krīḍitam atra dāsyati puro dāridram evottaram
children.translated_text: will give you nothing but poverty as the answer hereafter.

children.text: kandarpa-pratibhū-niveśita-valī-rekhā-āvalī-śobhite
līlā-udañcita-bāhu-pāśa-yugala-āpātaiś ca bhoḥ kāmukāḥ
veśyānāṃ vipule nitamba-phalake śāraiḥ kaṭākṣair ito
yad vaḥ krīḍitam atra dāsyati puro dāridram eva uttaram
śūlenādya mṛtāham adya sarajāḥ kartavyam adya vrataṃ
children.translated_text: 'I shall die today by a stake! Today there is a festival! A vow must be performed today!'

children.text: tyāgī nāsti tato 'dhiko 'para iti ślāghā vipakṣasya ca
children.translated_text: 'There is no greater giver than he!' — and praise of a rival too —

children.text: kaṃ cin notsahate sa rājatanayo jānāti mātā mamety
children.translated_text: 'A certain prince cannot bear it!' — 'My mother knows!' —

children.text: evaṃ mugdhabhujaṃga rūkṣagaṇikāvāco 'cirāc chroṣyasi
children.translated_text: Thus, O naive one, you will soon hear the harsh words of a heartless courtesan.

children.text: śūlena adya mṛta āham adya sa-rajāḥ kartavyam adya vrataṃ
tyāgī na asti tato 'dhiko 'para iti ślāghā vipakṣasya ca
kaṃ cin na utsahate sa rāja-tanayo jānāti mātā mama ity
evaṃ mugdha-bhujaṃga rūkṣa-gaṇikā-vāco 'cirāc chroṣyasi
mālinyaṃ prakaṭikaroti nibiḍaṃ nairguṇyam ātanvate(sī)
children.translated_text: She manifests dense impurity, she extends worthlessness,

children.text: jīrṇasnehaparamparā vidadhate pātre 'py aho dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: she causes old chains of affection to produce defamation even in a worthy vessel —

children.text: veśyā dīpaśikheva bhāti rajanau rūpabhramāndhīkṛto
children.translated_text: the courtesan shines like a lamp-flame in the night, blinding with the illusion of beauty,

children.text: yatrāyaṃ kurute pataṅgapatanaṃ hā hā bhujaṃgavrajaḥ
children.translated_text: where — alas, alas! — this swarm of naive ones performs the moth's plunge.

children.text: mālinyaṃ prakaṭi-karoti nibiḍaṃ nairguṇyam ātanvate(sī)
jīrṇa-sneha-paramparā vidadhate pātre 'py aho dūṣaṇam
veśyā dīpa-śikha īva bhāti rajanau rūpa-bhrama-andhīkṛto
yatra ayaṃ kurute pataṅga-patanaṃ hā hā bhujaṃga-vrajaḥ
keśākarṣaṇakarmaṇi vyavasitā vīryaṃ harantī paraṃ
children.translated_text: Engaged in the act of hair-pulling, stealing one's supreme vigor,

children.text: mlāniṃ kām api tanvatī smitamukhī lagnā ca karṇāntike
children.translated_text: producing a certain languor, smiling-faced and clinging to the ear,

children.text: utkampaṃ mativibhramaṃ vidadhatī yūnāṃ śanair ninditā
children.translated_text: causing trembling and bewilderment of mind in young men — gently reviled,

children.text: tāruṇyasya janāpavāda ... veśyā ca saṃdṛśyate
children.translated_text: the courtesan appears as the public scandal of youth...

children.text: keśa-ākarṣaṇa-karmaṇi vyavasitā vīryaṃ harantī paraṃ
mlāniṃ kām api tanvatī smita-mukhī lagnā ca karṇa-antike
utkampaṃ mati-vibhramaṃ vidadhatī yūnāṃ śanair ninditā
tāruṇyasya jana-apavāda ... veśyā ca saṃdṛśyate
yo 'yaṃ nirdayadantakhaṇḍanakaro buddhiprayogair haṭhān
children.translated_text: This merciless tooth-crushing technique, contrived forcefully through strategies of intellect,

children.text: nīrandhro bhujayantrapīḍanavidhiḥ sollāsam utpāditaḥ
children.translated_text: this procedure of squeezing in the arm-press with no gaps, produced with relish —

children.text: tenekṣor iva kāmukasya sarasasyādāya sāraṃ paraṃ
children.translated_text: by this, having extracted the supreme essence of the juicy lover as if from sugarcane,

children.text: veśyābhiḥ kriyate bahir yadi paraṃ niṣkāsanaṃ śalkavat
children.translated_text: the courtesans cast him out like the husk.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ nirdaya-danta-khaṇḍana-karo buddhi-prayogair haṭhān
nīrandhro bhuja-yantra-pīḍana-vidhiḥ sa-ullāsam utpāditaḥ
tena ikṣor iva kāmukasya sa-rasasyā adāya sāraṃ paraṃ
veśyābhiḥ kriyate bahir yadi paraṃ niṣkāsanaṃ śalkavat
vāgbhir bhartsanam aṃśukādiharaṇaṃ saṃtāḍanaṃ muṣṭibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Scolding with words, snatching away garments and the like, striking with fists,

children.text: kiṃ cānyad viparītadarśnam adhaskāro 'tha pādāhatiḥ
children.translated_text: and something more — displaying things upside-down, humiliation, and kicking with feet —

children.text: ityādi prathamaṃ yadeva surataprauḍhopacārakrame
children.translated_text: all that which was first [employed] in the sequence of bold love-making techniques,

children.text: veśyā paśyata tat tad eva kurute nirvāsane kāminām
children.translated_text: behold! the very same the courtesan employs in banishing her lovers.

children.text: vāgbhir bhartsanam aṃśuka-ādi-haraṇaṃ saṃtāḍanaṃ muṣṭibhiḥ
kiṃ ca anyad viparīta-darśnam adhas-kāro 'tha pāda-āhatiḥ
ity-ādi prathamaṃ yada īva surata-prauḍha-upacāra-krame
veśyā paśyata tat tad eva kurute nirvāsane kāminām
yad bhūyaḥ paricumbanaṃ yad asakṛtsarvāṅgam āliṅganaṃ
children.translated_text: That repeated kissing, that embrace of the entire body again and again,

children.text: yat paryutsukam īkṣitaṃ sarabhasaṃ yac cāṭukotkaṭṭanam(utkīrtanam?)
children.translated_text: that eager gazing, that passionate bursting-forth of flattery,

children.text: yat sadbhāvakathānakaṃ rahasi yat kiṃ cid abhyarthanaṃ
children.translated_text: that telling of feelings of sincerity in private, that certain entreaty —

children.text: veśyānāṃ viṣavat tad eva nipuṇaṃ cintyaṃ sadā kāmukaiḥ
children.translated_text: all that of courtesans should always be pondered by lovers as skillfully [administered] poison.

children.text: yad bhūyaḥ paricumbanaṃ yad asakṛt-sarva-aṅgam āliṅganaṃ
yat paryutsukam īkṣitaṃ sa-rabhasaṃ yac cāṭuka-utkaṭṭanam(utkīrtanam?)
yat sadbhāva-kathānakaṃ rahasi yat kiṃ cid abhyarthanaṃ
veśyānāṃ viṣa-vat tad eva nipuṇaṃ cintyaṃ sadā kāmukaiḥ
bibboke bakaceṣṭitaṃ bahuvidhabhrūvibhrameṣu bhramaṃ
children.translated_text: In coyness, the behavior of a crane; in the play of manifold eyebrow-movements, deception;

children.text: kauṭilyaṃ nakharakṣateṣu suratopāyeṣu māyāṃ svayam
children.translated_text: crookedness in nail-scratches; in the techniques of love-making, illusion itself;

children.text: sītkārāntarasatyam arthaharaṇaṃ sarvatra ye jānate
children.translated_text: truth within sighs, and theft of wealth everywhere — those who know

children.text: veśyānāṃ paramaṃ rahasyam avanau te ke 'pi medhāvinaḥ
children.translated_text: the supreme secret of courtesans, they are the rare wise ones on earth.

children.text: bibboke baka-ceṣṭitaṃ bahu-vidha-bhrū-vibhrameṣu bhramaṃ
kauṭilyaṃ nakhara-kṣateṣu surata-upāyeṣu māyāṃ svayam
sītkāra-antara-satyam artha-haraṇaṃ sarvatra ye jānate
veśyānāṃ paramaṃ rahasyam avanau te ke 'pi medhāvinaḥ
kiṃ cit prāhuṇakāgamena kim api prastāravistāravat
children.translated_text: By some pretext of a guest's arrival, by some elaborate conversation,

children.text: yātrācaitratithikramaiḥ kim api ca krodhaprasādodayaiḥ
children.translated_text: by pilgrimages and festivals and changes of season, by outbursts of anger and displays of favor,

children.text: kiṃ cit kāñcanaratnavastraviṣayair nānāvidhair dohadair
children.translated_text: by certain cravings for gold, gems, garments, and various other desires —

children.text: dvārāṇy arthavinirgamasya gaṇikāḥ kurvanti śṛṅgāriṇām
children.translated_text: courtesans create doorways for the outflow of wealth from their amorous ones.

children.text: kiṃ cit prāhuṇaka-āgamena kim api prastāra-vistāra-vat
yātrā-caitra-tithi-kramaiḥ kim api ca krodha-prasāda-udayaiḥ
kiṃ cit kāñcana-ratna-vastra-viṣayair nānā-vidhair dohadair
dvārāṇy artha-vinirgamasya gaṇikāḥ kurvanti śṛṅgāriṇām
arthuṣmā pitṛlālanaṃ viṭaghaṭāmelaḥ priyammanyatā
children.translated_text: The warmth of wealth, fondling of parents, association with bands of libertines, the conceit of being the beloved,

children.text: tāruṇyaṃ nagare sthitis taralatā dhiḥ kāmaśāstraṃ prati
children.translated_text: youth, residence in the city, fickleness, devotion to the <s>Kāmaśāstra</s> (treatise on love),

children.text: saṅgītaṃ rajanī vidhur madhumadaḥ spardhā sapatnais tathā
children.translated_text: music, the night, the moon, the intoxication of liquor, rivalry with co-wives —

children.text: veśyānām anuraktavittaharaṇe kurvanti sāhāyakam
children.translated_text: these assist courtesans in stealing the wealth of an enamored man.

children.text: arth-uṣmā pitṛ-lālanaṃ viṭa-ghaṭā-melaḥ priyam-manyatā
tāruṇyaṃ nagare sthitis taralatā dhiḥ kāma-śāstraṃ prati
saṅgītaṃ rajanī vidhur madhu-madaḥ spardhā sa-patnais tathā
veśyānām anurakta-vitta-haraṇe kurvanti sāhāyakam
vaidagdhīm avadhīraya vyavahitaṃ kāryaṃ kalākauśalaṃ
children.translated_text: Disregard cleverness! Skill in arts is an irrelevant matter!

children.text: saujanyena gataṃ kim anyad aphalo rāśir guṇānām api
children.translated_text: What has gone through nobility? Even a fruitless heap of virtues amounts to nothing —

children.text: yasmān na praṇayena na praṇatibhiḥ premṇā na na prīṇanair
children.translated_text: since not by affection, not by prostrations, not by love, not by pleasuring,

children.text: na prāṇair api te bhujaṃga gaṇikā vittaṃ vinā tuṣyati
children.translated_text: not even by your very life-breath, O naive one, is a courtesan satisfied without wealth.

children.text: vaidagdhīm avadhīraya vyavahitaṃ kāryaṃ kalā-kauśalaṃ
saujanyena gataṃ kim anyad aphalo rāśir guṇānām api
yasmān na praṇayena na praṇatibhiḥ premṇā na na prīṇanair
na prāṇair api te bhujaṃga gaṇikā vittaṃ vinā tuṣyati
dāsī nātha tavāham eva vibhavaḥ sarvas tvadīyaḥ sthito
children.translated_text: 'I am your slave, O lord! All wealth is yours and stands [at your disposal]!

children.text: mā māṃ nirdaya muñca śūnyam akhilaṃ manye jagat tvāṃ vinā
children.translated_text: Do not abandon me, O merciless one! I consider the whole world empty without you!' —

children.text: ity uktvā sahasā bhujaṅgapurato yad veśyayā rudyate
children.translated_text: when a courtesan weeps thus suddenly before a naive man,

children.text: bhuktocchiṣṭadaridrakāmivibhavās te kevalaṃ tad viduḥ
children.translated_text: only those whose wealth is like the leftover scraps of a poor beggar understand that.

children.text: dāsī nātha tava aham eva vibhavaḥ sarvas tvadīyaḥ sthito
mā māṃ nirdaya muñca śūnyam akhilaṃ manye jagat tvāṃ vinā
ity uktvā sahasā bhujaṅga-purato yad veśyayā rudyate
bhukta-ucchiṣṭa-daridra-kāmi-vibhavās te kevalaṃ tad viduḥ
svapne kām api saṃsmaran priya mayā dṛṣṭo 'si tat te balād
children.translated_text: 'In a dream I recalled some woman — but it was you, O beloved, that I saw! And that was by your power alone!'

children.text: evaṃ māṃ prati sāṃprataṃ kim ucitā niṣkāraṇaṃ vañcanā
children.translated_text: 'Is such deception toward me now fitting, [done] without reason?'

children.text: taj jāgarmi varaṃ niśāsu yad asau nidrāpi me drohiṇīty
children.translated_text: 'Therefore I shall stay awake at night, for even sleep is my enemy!' —

children.text: ālāpair gaṇikāgaṇena na ca ko viśvāsyate kāmukaḥ
children.translated_text: by such words of the courtesan band, which lover is not taken into confidence?

children.text: svapne kām api saṃsmaran priya mayā dṛṣṭo 'si tat te balād
evaṃ māṃ prati sāṃprataṃ kim ucitā niṣkāraṇaṃ vañcanā
taj jāgarmi varaṃ niśāsu yad asau nidrā āpi me drohiṇi īty
ālāpair gaṇikā-gaṇena na ca ko viśvāsyate kāmukaḥ
bhrūbhaṅgair atibhaṅguraiḥ kuṭilitaprāntas tathā kuntalaiḥ
children.translated_text: With exceedingly fickle frownings of eyebrows, with curling locks twisted at their tips,

children.text: sopekṣair iva cakṣuṣoḥ saralitāpāṅgaiś ca bhaṅgyantaraiḥ
children.translated_text: with seemingly attentive eyes whose corners are drawn out straight, and with other gestures —

children.text: ātmīyāṃ calacittavṛttiracanāṃ veśyā varākī sadā
children.translated_text: the poor courtesan constantly displays to young men her own composition of fickle-minded behavior,

children.text: yūnāṃ darśayatīva te yadi paraṃ mūḍhā na taj jānate
children.translated_text: yet the foolish ones, even so, do not recognize it.

children.text: bhrū-bhaṅgair atibhaṅguraiḥ kuṭilita-prāntas tathā kuntalaiḥ
sa-upekṣair iva cakṣuṣoḥ saralita-apāṅgaiś ca bhaṅgy-antaraiḥ
ātmīyāṃ cala-citta-vṛtti-racanāṃ veśyā varākī sadā
yūnāṃ darśayati iva te yadi paraṃ mūḍhā na taj jānate
vakroktyā prathamaṃ nirādaratayā paścāt tataḥ kena cid
children.translated_text: First by evasive speech, then by indifference — and then with someone else

children.text: dātavyaṃ bahu tatra yāmi bhavatām(tād) bhūyo 'pi nau saṃgamaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Much must be given there; I shall go there; but we shall meet again!' —

children.text: ity ukto 'pi na budhyate khalu yadā rāgī daridro jaḍaś
children.translated_text: even when told thus, the poor, dull-witted, infatuated man does not understand,

children.text: ceṭībhir bahubhāṣitair api tadā hastārgalair vāryate
children.translated_text: and then he is restrained by the maidservants with much talking and with arm-barriers.

children.text: vakra-uktyā prathamaṃ nirādaratayā paścāt tataḥ kena cid
dātavyaṃ bahu tatra yāmi bhavatām(tād) bhūyo 'pi nau saṃgamaḥ
ity ukto 'pi na budhyate khalu yadā rāgī daridro jaḍaś
ceṭībhir bahu-bhāṣitair api tadā hasta-argalair vāryate
bhūyaḥ kālavaśāt tam arjitadhanaṃ dṛṣṭvātha madvallabhaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Again, seeing him who has earned wealth through the force of time — «He is my beloved!»'

children.text: saḥ kruddho gamitas tvayeti kalaho mātrā samaṃ jāyate
children.translated_text: '«He was sent away angry by you!»' — thus a quarrel with the mother arises;

children.text: kṛtvā taṃ prati ca vratādi virahaṃ svaṃ nāṭayitvā tatas
children.translated_text: then, performing vows and the like toward him and displaying her own [feigned] separation,

children.text: tasmin mitramukhena saṃdhir aparo veśyābhir utpādyate
children.translated_text: another reconciliation is contrived by the courtesans through the mouth of a friend.

children.text: bhūyaḥ kāla-vaśāt tam arjita-dhanaṃ dṛṣṭva ātha mad-vallabhaḥ
saḥ kruddho gamitas tvaya īti kalaho mātrā samaṃ jāyate
kṛtvā taṃ prati ca vrata-ādi virahaṃ svaṃ nāṭayitvā tatas
tasmin mitra-mukhena saṃdhir aparo veśyābhir utpādyate
prauḍha prāṇada kānta nātha subhagodāra priya tvāṃ vinā
children.translated_text: 'O bold one! O life-giver! O handsome one! O lord! O fortunate, noble, beloved one! Without you,

children.text: kiṃ vittena gṛheṇa kiṃ kim asubhir hyo 'pīti yo bhāṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: what use is wealth? What use is a house? What use are life-breaths? Even yesterday...' — thus he was addressed;

children.text: tasyaivādya nirāśa durbhaga paśo nirlajja gacchādhunā
children.translated_text: and that very same one is now told: 'O hopeless one! O wretch! O beast! O shameless one! Go now!

children.text: dhik tvāṃ nirdhanacaṅgam ity apavadan hrīto na veśyājanaḥ
children.translated_text: Fie upon you, penniless vagabond!' — thus courtesans rail without any shame.

children.text: prauḍha prāṇa-da kānta nātha subhaga udāra priya tvāṃ vinā
kiṃ vittena gṛheṇa kiṃ kim asubhir hyo 'pi iti yo bhāṣitaḥ
tasya eva adya nirāśa durbhaga paśo nirlajja gaccha adhunā
dhik tvāṃ nirdhana-caṅgam ity apavadan hrīto na veśyā-janaḥ
ke cid dyūtakarā bhavanti katicid bhikṣācarāḥ kiṅkarāḥ
children.translated_text: Some become gamblers, some become beggars and servants,

children.text: ke cit karmakarāḥ pare dhanavatāṃ ślāghākarāḥ ke cana
children.translated_text: some become laborers, others become flatterers of the wealthy,

children.text: skandhāsaktapaṭaccarā dya(a)nucarā śokād akiṃcitkarās
children.translated_text: with rags slung over their shoulders, wretched followers, worthless in their grief —

children.text: te 'mī kāmivarāḥ purā samabhavan veśyāsu ye gocarāḥ
children.translated_text: these are those excellent lovers who once were the devotees of courtesans.

children.text: ke cid dyūta-karā bhavanti kati-cid bhikṣā-carāḥ kiṅkarāḥ
ke cit karma-karāḥ pare dhanavatāṃ ślāghā-karāḥ ke cana
skandha-āsakta-paṭac-carā dya(a)nucarā śokād a-kiṃ-cit-karās
te 'mī kāmi-varāḥ purā samabhavan veśyāsu ye gocarāḥ
veśyābhir vivaśīkṛtaḥ kupuruṣaḥ saṃjāyate durgato
children.translated_text: A worthless man, brought under the power of courtesans, falls into misfortune;

children.text: daurgatyena durodare nipatitaḥ svaṃ hārayaty eva sa
children.translated_text: through misfortune he falls into desperate gambling and loses everything he has;

children.text: ruddho dyūtakaraiḥ karoti vidhuraś cauryaṃ tatas taskaro
children.translated_text: cornered by gamblers, the wretched one turns to theft — then, a thief,

children.text: vadhyaḥ syān nṛpater aho nu viṣayāsakter durantā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: he becomes fit to be executed by the king. Alas! The course of attachment to pleasures is endless.

children.text: veśyābhir vivaśī-kṛtaḥ kupuruṣaḥ saṃjāyate durgato
daurgatyena durodare nipatitaḥ svaṃ hārayaty eva sa
ruddho dyūta-karaiḥ karoti vidhuraś cauryaṃ tatas taskaro
vadhyaḥ syān nṛpater aho nu viṣaya-āsakter durantā gatiḥ
ājīvaḥ kapaṭānurāgakalayā doṣo na duḥśīlatā
children.translated_text: Their livelihood is through a web of feigned love; their vice is not licentiousness;

children.text: vaidhavyaṃ na ca bādhate sadasatoḥ saṃbḥāvanā vyatyayāt
children.translated_text: widowhood does not afflict them; the estimation of good and bad is reversed;

children.text: yatkimcitkaraṇe parasvaharaṇe vrīḍā na pīḍākarī
children.translated_text: in doing whatever they please, in taking others' property, shame causes no distress;

children.text: no vā rājabhayaṃ ca hī bata sukhaṃ jīvanti vārastriyas=
children.translated_text: nor is there fear of the king — alas! how happily the women of pleasure live!

children.text: ājīvaḥ kapaṭa-anurāga-kalayā doṣo na duḥśīlatā
vaidhavyaṃ na ca bādhate sad-asatoḥ saṃbḥāvanā vyatyayāt
yat-kim-cit-karaṇe para-sva-haraṇe vrīḍā na pīḍā-karī
na u vā rāja-bhayaṃ ca hī bata sukhaṃ jīvanti vāra-striyas=
strīti prītikaraṃ puraḥ pariṇatau hālāhalaṃ kevalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Woman' — a word that is pleasing at first, but in the end nothing but <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison);

children.text: sarvasya vyasanaṃ kilaitad adhikaṃ tatrāpi veśyeti ca
children.translated_text: this is truly the supreme vice of all — and the courtesan is worse still;

children.text: prādhānyena tatas tad eva kathitaṃ yat tatprasaṅgena ca
children.translated_text: therefore what has been principally told concerns her, and what has been expounded

children.text: vyākhyātaṃ guṇadoṣajātam ucitaṃ cintyaṃ tad apy ādarāt
children.translated_text: by way of her regarding the nature of virtues and faults is worthy of careful consideration.

children.text: stri īti prīti-karaṃ puraḥ pariṇatau hālāhalaṃ kevalaṃ
sarvasya vyasanaṃ kila etad adhikaṃ tatra api veśya īti ca
prādhānyena tatas tad eva kathitaṃ yat tat-prasaṅgena ca
vyākhyātaṃ guṇa-doṣa-jātam ucitaṃ cintyaṃ tad apy ādarāt
cetaḥśvāpadavāgurā daśaguṇasphārasmaroḍḍāmarāḥ
children.translated_text: The trap for the wild beast of the mind, the ten-quality-wide uproar of <s>Smara</s> (Kāma, god of love),

children.text: kartavyāvadhayaḥ(?) samudralaharīpūrair ivotpāditāḥ
children.translated_text: the limits of what should be done, raised up as if by the floods of ocean waves —

children.text: nāpi svāmyasamarpaṇena na sakhe sakhyā (?) virodhena vā
children.translated_text: neither by surrendering ownership, nor O friend, through friendship, nor through enmity,

children.text: gūḍhāntarmukhasāhasavyatikarārakṣyāḥ paraṃ yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: but only through the inner secrecy of daring courage — thus women are to be guarded.

children.text: cetaḥ-śvāpada-vāgurā daśa-guṇa-sphāra-smara-uḍḍāmarāḥ
kartavyāvadhayaḥ(?) samudra-laharī-pūrair iva utpāditāḥ
na api svāmy-asamarpaṇena na sakhe sakhyā (?) virodhena vā
gūḍha-antarmukha-sāhasa-vyatikarā-rakṣyāḥ paraṃ yoṣitaḥ
bhasmasnānamahāvrataṃ katipayaśrībhraṣṭasaṃbhāvitaṃ
children.translated_text: Bathing in ashes, the great vow, honored by a few who have lost their fortune,

children.text: sarvāpahnavahastalāghavakalākūṭākṣaśikṣātmakam
children.translated_text: consisting of the art of denying everything, sleight of hand, deceptive glance-techniques —

children.text: pratyāśāpunaruktahāraṇajagaddrohaṃ vivādāspadaṃ
children.translated_text: repeated swindling of expectations, worldwide treachery, a ground for disputes,

children.text: dāridryasya nimantraṇaṃ kim aparaṃ dhig dyūtalīlāyitam
children.translated_text: an invitation to poverty — fie upon the pastime of gambling! What more [can be said]?

children.text: bhasma-snāna-mahā-vrataṃ katipaya-śrī-bhraṣṭa-saṃbhāvitaṃ
sarva-apahnava-hasta-lāghava-kalā-kūṭa-akṣa-śikṣā-ātmakam
pratyāśā-punarukta-hāraṇa-jagad-drohaṃ vivāda-āspadaṃ
dāridryasya nimantraṇaṃ kim aparaṃ dhig dyūta-līlāyitam
hiṃsānirghṛṇakarmabhūḥ pratipadānekapramādaprasūs
children.translated_text: A field for the merciless work of violence, producing manifold dangers at every step,

children.text: avyāpāradhurandharā pratikṛtā grāmyair jaghanyaiḥ śvabhiḥ
children.translated_text: bearing the yoke of uselessness, imitated by base village-dogs,

children.text: śūnyāraṇyasadāpravāsavirasavyāyāmamithyāguṇāḥ
children.translated_text: [consisting of] the dismal virtues of constant exile in empty wilderness, wearying exertion, and falsehood —

children.text: kāyakleśaphalāvadhir matimatāṃ sevyā mṛgavyāpi kim
children.translated_text: The limit of fruits obtained through bodily toil — should it be sought by the wise? What use is hunting?

children.text: hiṃsā-nirghṛṇa-karma-bhūḥ pratipada āneka-pramāda-prasūs
avyāpāra-dhurandharā pratikṛtā grāmyair jaghanyaiḥ śvabhiḥ
śūnya-āraṇya-sadā-pravāsa-virasa-vyāyāma-mithyā-guṇāḥ
kāya-kleśa-phala-avadhir matimatāṃ sevyā mṛgavya āpi kim
śaucācāravicāravāhyam akhilākāryāhitācāryakaṃ
children.translated_text: Bereft of cleanliness, conduct, and judgment, the teacher of everything that should not be done and of harm,

children.text: tattadgopyarahasyamantrabhiduraṃ nirnaiśam akṣṇos tamaḥ
children.translated_text: breaching all that is confidential — secrets and counsels, perpetual darkness of the eyes,

children.text: yattadvāddakalipramādavividhonmādaiḥ piśācāyitaṃ
children.translated_text: that which, through quarrels, heedlessness, and various kinds of madness, makes one demon-possessed —

children.text: madyaṃ mūrtam amedhyam etad itarād anyasya kasya priyam
children.translated_text: liquor, impurity incarnate — to whom other than a wretch is this dear?

children.text: śauca-ācāra-vicāra-vāhyam akhila-akārya-ahita-acāryakaṃ
tat-tad-gopya-rahasya-mantra-bhiduraṃ nirnaiśam akṣṇos tamaḥ
yat-tad-vādda-kali-pramāda-vividha-unmādaiḥ piśācāyitaṃ
madyaṃ mūrtam amedhyam etad itarād anyasya kasya priyam
ulkāpātasahodaraṃ sahacaraṃ naidāghajhañjhāmarut
children.translated_text: Sibling of a falling meteor, companion of the scorching summer storm,

children.text: jhampānāṃ harakaṇṭhalālitagaradroṇīkuṭumbīkṛtam
children.translated_text: of raging torrents, domesticated in the poison-trough caressed by <s>Hara's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) throat,

children.text: jihvāgre karapattramitram aniśaṃ tat karkaśaṃ durvaco
children.translated_text: a saw-like friend on the tip of the tongue, always that rough, unbearable speech —

children.text: yasyāste vada kadvadaḥ katham aho sa api svayaṃ jīvati
children.translated_text: tell me, the harsh-speaker who possesses this — how, alas, does even he himself live?

children.text: ulkā-pāta-sahodaraṃ sahacaraṃ naidāgha-jhañjhā-marut
jhampānāṃ hara-kaṇṭha-lālita-gara-droṇī-kuṭumbī-kṛtam
jihvā-agre kara-pattra-mitram aniśaṃ tat karkaśaṃ durvaco
yasyā aste vada kad-vadaḥ katham aho sa api svayaṃ jīvati
caṇḍaṃ daṇḍam akāṇḍa eva kalayan rājā prajānāṃ yamaḥ
children.translated_text: The king who inflicts fierce punishment even without cause is <s>Yama</s> (the god of death) to his subjects;

children.text: kurvan durvyayam arthadūṣaṇaruciḥ svasyaiva sa drohakṛt
children.translated_text: making wasteful expenditure, delighting in the corruption of wealth, he is the betrayer of himself.

children.text: saumyaḥ saumyakaro 'tiviśvanayanānando 'bhinandyaḥ satāṃ
children.translated_text: The gentle one, who brings gentleness, the exceeding delight that pleases the eyes of the entire world, to be celebrated by the virtuous,

children.text: saśrīkaḥ kamalākaraś ca suṣamāṃ kāṃ kām aho nārhati
children.translated_text: prosperous, and like a lake of lotuses — what beauty, alas, does he not deserve?

children.text: caṇḍaṃ daṇḍam akāṇḍa eva kalayan rājā prajānāṃ yamaḥ
kurvan durvyayam artha-dūṣaṇa-ruciḥ svasya eva sa droha-kṛt
saumyaḥ saumya-karo 'tiviśva-nayana-ānando 'bhinandyaḥ satāṃ
sa-śrīkaḥ kamala-ākaraś ca suṣamāṃ kāṃ kām aho na arhati
saṃsārasya maheśvaro dinapatir dhvāntasya vaidyo rujāṃ
children.translated_text: The great lord of worldly existence, the sun for darkness, the physician for diseases,

children.text: prāyaścittam aghasya śāstram aparijñānasya toyaṃ tṛṣaḥ
children.translated_text: the expiation for sin, the treatise for ignorance, the water for thirst,

children.text: siddhājñā garalasya tīrthasaraṇaṃ vṛddhatvavaiklavyayoḥ
children.translated_text: the perfected remedy for poison, the pilgrimage-refuge for old age and affliction,

children.text: saptāṅgavyasanāvaleḥ praśamanopāyaś ca śikṣā satām
children.translated_text: and the means of pacifying the series of seven-limbed calamities — such is the training of the virtuous.

children.text: saṃsārasya maheśvaro dina-patir dhvāntasya vaidyo rujāṃ
prāyaścittam aghasya śāstram aparijñānasya toyaṃ tṛṣaḥ
siddha-ājñā garalasya tīrtha-saraṇaṃ vṛddhatva-vaiklavyayoḥ
saptāṅga-vyasana-āvaleḥ praśamana-upāyaś ca śikṣā satām
oṃkāraḥ sāhasānāṃ nijaguṇanipuṇapratyavekṣā sukhānāṃ
children.translated_text: The inauguration of bold ventures, the keen recognition of one's own merits — [the source] of pleasures,

children.text: kādācitkaḥ prayogaḥ sakalaparicayopādhivaidagdhyabandhuḥ
children.translated_text: an occasional endeavor, the kinsman of expertise born of all manner of acquaintance,

children.text: kaṣṭānām antyakāṣṭhā dhanarasikavaṇiglokayātrāprasaṅgo
children.translated_text: the ultimate limit of hardships, the occasion for the worldly journey of merchants who delight in wealth,

children.text: jīvajjanmāntaraṃ cety alam atibahunā svasti deśāntarāya
children.translated_text: and another birth for the living — enough of too much [talk]! May it be well with foreign lands!

children.text: oṃkāraḥ sāhasānāṃ nija-guṇa-nipuṇa-pratyavekṣā sukhānāṃ
kādācitkaḥ prayogaḥ sakala-paricaya-upādhi-vaidagdhya-bandhuḥ
kaṣṭānām antya-kāṣṭhā dhana-rasika-vaṇig-lokayātrā-prasaṅgo
jīvaj-janma-antaraṃ ca ity alam atibahunā svasti deśa-antarāya
yady apy asti savistarādbhutakathābhūyiṣṭhanānāvidha
children.translated_text: Although there are extensive tales, filled with wonder, of many kinds,

children.text: vyākhyāyāṃ niravadyahṛdyacaritodāraṃ ca deśāntaram
children.translated_text: and foreign lands appear noble with blameless and pleasing ways in description,

children.text: tatrāpi svagṛheṣu guṇavadgoṣṭhīgariṣṭhīkṛta
children.translated_text: even so, at home, enriched by assemblies of the virtuous,

children.text: sphāro 'nāratabhāratīrasapariṣyandaḥ sakhe sundaraḥ
children.translated_text: the abundant, unceasing overflow of the nectar of <s>Bhāratī</s> (learning), O friend, is beautiful.

children.text: yady apy asti sa-vistara-adbhuta-kathā-bhūyiṣṭha-nānā-vidha
vyākhyāyāṃ niravadya-hṛdya-carita-udāraṃ ca deśa-antaram
tatra api sva-gṛheṣu guṇavad-goṣṭhī-gariṣṭhī-kṛta
sphāro 'nārata-bhāratī-rasa-pariṣyandaḥ sakhe sundaraḥ
te vandyā makarandabindumadhurair abhyutthitād akṣarair
children.translated_text: Venerable are they, from whose syllables rise, sweet as drops of nectar,

children.text: yeṣā vānti sarasvatīparimalodgārā mukhāmbhoruhāt
children.translated_text: from whose lotus-mouths blow forth the fragrant exhalations of <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: vandyās te 'pi tadantarālapatitā ye bhṛṅgabhaṅgījuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: venerable too are those who fall in between them, who partake of the bee's manner —

children.text: sāndrānandakarambitaṃ jagad idaṃ vindanti nindanti ca
children.translated_text: they find and censure this world steeped in dense delight.

children.text: te vandyā makaranda-bindu-madhurair abhyutthitād akṣarair
yeṣā vānti sarasvatī-parimala-udgārā mukha-ambho-ruhāt
vandyās te 'pi tad-antarāla-patitā ye bhṛṅga-bhaṅgī-juṣaḥ
sāndra-ānanda-karambitaṃ jagad idaṃ vindanti nindanti ca
dṛṣṭvā deśam aśeṣam ā jalanidher ālokya kautūhalād
children.translated_text: Having seen the entire land up to the ocean, having gazed with curiosity

children.text: āsthānīr avanībhṛtāṃ ca punar apy āgatya deśaṃ nijam
children.translated_text: upon the courts of kings, and then returning again to one's own land,

children.text: kāruṇyāt taruṇaṃ janaṃ prati satām abhyarthanābhis tathā
children.translated_text: out of compassion for the young, at the entreaties of the good, accordingly

children.text: so 'yaṃ saṃprati Jalhaṇena kavinā Mudghopadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: this <s>Mugdhopadeśa</s> (Instruction for the Naive) has now been composed by the poet <s>Jalhaṇa</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā deśam aśeṣam ā jalanidher ālokya kautūhalād
āsthānīr avanībhṛtāṃ ca punar apy āgatya deśaṃ nijam
kāruṇyāt taruṇaṃ janaṃ prati satām abhyarthanābhis tathā
so 'yaṃ saṃprati Jalhaṇena kavinā Mudghopadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ
vidyābhyāsaparamparāparicayair bālyaṃ kṛtārthīkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: Childhood was made fruitful through successive acquaintance with the study of knowledge;

children.text: tāruṇyaṃ taruṇīnirantaraparīrambhaiś ca saṃbhāvitam
children.translated_text: youth was honored through unceasing embraces of young women;

children.text: asmākaṃ surasindhurodhasi punaḥ śaṃbhāvadaṃbhārcanair
children.translated_text: for us, on the bank of the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), through sincere worship of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: vṛddhatvasya viśuddhatāṃ janayituṃ kartavyaśeṣaḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: the remaining duty stands — to produce the purity of old age.

children.text: vidyā-abhyāsa-paramparā-paricayair bālyaṃ kṛta-arthī-kṛtaṃ
tāruṇyaṃ taruṇī-nirantara-parīrambhaiś ca saṃbhāvitam
asmākaṃ sura-sindhu-rodhasi punaḥ śaṃbhāva-daṃbha-arcanair
vṛddhatvasya viśuddhatāṃ janayituṃ kartavya-śeṣaḥ sthitaḥ
